Offenses known to police and reported to the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting program, per 100,000 residents. A city's values are its police department's. A county's values add up every police agency the FBI lists in the county (city police, the sheriff, campus and state police posts): a department that serves several counties is divided among them by where its residents live, and agencies the FBI places in no county, such as most state police, are left out. Because jurisdictions overlap and some agencies report incompletely, county figures are approximate, and a county's year is shown only when agencies serving at least 75% of its residents reported every month. State and national values cover the agencies that reported (see the coverage row). Violent crime is murder, rape, robbery and aggravated assault; property crime is burglary, larceny-theft and motor vehicle theft. The FBI advises comparing a city with its state and a state with the nation rather than ranking places; the figures also depend on how often crimes are reported to police.
Source: FBI Crime Data Explorer, Uniform Crime Reporting Program.
